title: Investigate whether encrusted/package.json is vestigial upstream cruft
description: Found during the h2g2-cwr audit (2026-06-16). encrusted/package.json is the upstream demille/encrusted project's OWN webpack playground: it pulls react@16, d3@3, redux, react-router@4, wasm-ffi, popper.js, and webpack/webpack-dev-server, with scripts (bundle, dev, build:debug/release producing web.wasm) that this project does not use. The real frontend is apps/web (Vite) and the real WASM is the wasm/ crate (h2g2_wasm.wasm via build.sh/just). If nothing invokes these scripts, the entire encrusted npm dependency tree is dead weight and likely the source of most of the ~123 GitHub security alerts (old react16/webpack4-era transitive deps). Action: confirm no build path uses encrusted's npm package, then delete encrusted/package.json + package-lock.json + webpack configs (or pare to the cargo-only bits). Related: [[h2g2-1g6]] (webpack-cli peer conflict lives in this same tree).
close_reason: Confirmed vestigial and removed. encrusted/package.json had no real build path: its scripts referenced nonexistent webpack.*.js configs, there was zero JS/frontend source, and the only build reference to encrusted is 'cd encrusted && cargo test' (Cargo, not npm). The engine is consumed purely as a Rust crate (wasm/ depends on encrusted via path; game data h2g2.z3 and invisiclues.json are include_bytes!/include_str! embedded). Deleted package.json + package-lock.json + 144M node_modules; encrusted is now cargo-only. 27 cargo tests still pass. This removes the react16/d3/webpack4-era tree behind most of the ~123 security alerts.

title: Resolve encrusted webpack-cli/webpack peer-dependency conflict
description: Tech debt found during PR integration (2026-06-16). encrusted/package.json pins webpack@^5.104.1 but webpack-cli@^3.2.3, which only supports webpack@4. npm install/ci fails without --legacy-peer-deps. Bump webpack-cli to 5.x (webpack-5 compatible) and verify the webpack bundle (npm run bundle) still builds. Note: copy-webpack-plugin and terser-webpack-plugin were already bumped to webpack-5-compatible versions (14.x / 5.x) in the recent dependabot batch.

title: Build CI/CD pipeline: lint, clippy, build-size checks
description: Product objective (Automated Confidence / Streamlined Review). Implement comprehensive CI checks to automate routine code-quality verification: ESLint (web), cargo clippy (Rust), build-size budget, and the full test suite (cargo test + vitest). Goal is to enable safe rapid merging of Dependabot and feature PRs.

title: Review deleted code from cleanup phase
description:
Audit the code that was deleted during the aggressive cleanup:
1. main.web.rs - was this truly unused?
2. Debug command infrastructure - verify these aren't needed
3. Debug implementation functions - check if any are still referenced
4. Terminal run() function - confirm only WASM is used

Ensure nothing critical was removed that breaks game functionality.
close_reason: Audit complete. Game functionality fully intact: lib builds clean, 27 cargo tests + 8 save/load integration tests pass, WASM build and apps/web (36 vitest) work. The upstream WASM-only cleanup was correct: (1) main.web.rs - gone, zero references, was a terminal/upstream-web entry not used by the WASM path; (2) debug-command REPL infrastructure - gone, no Debugger/DebugCmd/mod debug references remain; (3) debug implementation functions - debug_object_details/debug_history were still present but unreferenced (orphaned), now removed; (4) terminal run() - gone, encrusted is lib-only ([lib], no [[bin]]), WASM is the only consumer via wasm/src/lib.rs. Remediated two cleanup leftovers in 32fd3e94 (orphan debug fns + broken check:term/test npm scripts). Filed h2g2-tqe for the larger finding: encrusted/package.json appears to be vestigial upstream webpack/react16 cruft.

title: Add WASM integration tests
description:
Create tests to verify:
1. WASM module loads without errors
2. Game initialization (create()) succeeds
3. Game loop functions work (step, feed, get_updates)
4. Save/load functionality works
5. Undo/redo operations work

This is critical for beta stability - we cannot ship without verifying the core game engine actually works.

title: Simplify terminal control bar CSS
description: The TerminalControls component has evolved through multiple CSS approaches. Consolidate color styling, clarify the light background issue, and ensure the theme colors resolve correctly. Consider moving complex color logic to CSS variables or a dedicated stylesheet.

title: Package as a BYO template repo (clone, add game + hints, deploy)
description: Part of [[h2g2-dwd]]. Shape the project so the wasm/ + apps/web + engine stack is a reusable template: documented slots for {story.z3, hints.json}, build via just, deploy to Pages. h2g2 becomes the flagship populated instance. Optionally also publish the engine + hint system as a crate for Rust devs later. Decide repo split (separate template repo vs h2g2-as-template).

title: Ship a demo content pack on a freely-licensed v3 game
description: Part of [[h2g2-dwd]]. Pick a freely/openly-licensed v3 z-code game from the IF Archive (NOT Infocom IP) and author a small tagged hints.json for it, to demo the BYO experience end-to-end without any copyright exposure. Serves as the worked example DIYers copy.

title: Decouple game + hints from the VM core (runtime-loaded content pair)
description: Foundational refactor for [[h2g2-dwd]]. Replace the two compile-time bindings (game.rs include_bytes! h2g2.z3; hints.rs include_str! invisiclues.json) with runtime loading of a {story.z3, hints.json} pair passed in from the wasm/app layer. Move h2g2-specific content (game file, invisiclues.json, room ASCII art) out of the encrusted VM crate and up into the app/content layer, leaving encrusted a clean, data-general v3 z-machine + game-agnostic Invisiclues engine. Also lift the inline 'hint' command interception (zmachine.rs ~1453) and the HintSystem/AsciiArt fields out of the VM core so the engine is reusable. Good hygiene regardless of whether we ever publish.
acceptance_criteria: encrusted crate compiles with no embedded game/hints; wasm/ supplies story+hints at runtime; h2g2 still plays identically; all cargo + vitest tests pass.

title: Document the Invisiclues hint JSON schema (public BYO contract)
description: Part of [[h2g2-dwd]]. Write a clear spec + JSON Schema for the hints file: HintBook -> sections -> questions {question, answers[] (progressive levels), section, tags[]}; the act:/loc: tag conventions; how loc: tags map to room names from global-var-0; and the graceful-degradation behavior (untagged -> flat menu). This schema is the actual public contract DIYers author against.

title: BYO contextual-Invisiclues z-machine player (shareable, no catalog distribution)
description: Extract h2g2's engine into a shareable, bring-your-own-content interactive-fiction player whose differentiator is contextual Invisiclues hints. Users supply their own v3 .z3 story file and their own hints JSON; we distribute software only, never Infocom games or hint text. h2g2 becomes the flagship instance/template populated with its own content.
design:
DECISIONS (2026-06-16):
- BYO content only. Do NOT distribute the Infocom catalog or their Invisiclues (Activision IP). Ship software; users bring their own .z3 + hints.json. Legally identical to how Frotz/Parchment ship.
- v3 scope is intentional, not a limitation: the Invisiclues canon is the Infocom v3 era.
- Differentiator = the hint LAYER, not the VM. Nobody else surfaces Invisiclues contextually by location; existing tools (PRIZM, SLAG) ship separate menu-driven hint .z files. Our act:/loc: tag-scored surfacing is novel.
- Already general (verified): Zmachine::new() takes arbitrary story bytes; HintSystem (HintBook/Section/Question) is game-agnostic; get_current_room() reads global var 0 (Infocom convention) so location detection needs no per-game code. Only coupling is two compile-time include_* lines (game.rs embeds h2g2.z3, hints.rs embeds invisiclues.json).
- Graceful degradation lowers DIY barrier: untagged questions -> flat Invisiclues menu for free; add act:/loc: tags -> contextual surfacing.
- Authoring aid synergy: the object-tree inspector idea ([[h2g2-jqx]]) doubles as the tool for discovering room names to write loc: tags.
- Packaging: template repo ('clone, drop in your game + hints, deploy') is the primary deliverable since the value is the web terminal experience; optionally publish the engine as a crate later.
- Landscape verified via search: SLAG/PRIZM (separate hint .z files), Infocom Solid Gold (5 games with baked-in hints). None integrate contextual hints into an arbitrary-game web interpreter.
notes: Speculative/exploratory; captured per discussion, not committed. Related cleanup that preceded this: [[h2g2-tqe]] (removed vestigial encrusted npm), and the fork-divergence doc in encrusted/README.md.

title: Optional: d3 object-tree / world-map debug inspector (?debug)
description: Net-new idea salvaged from upstream demille/encrusted's old web playground (which is gone; do NOT revive the old react16/d3/wasm-ffi code). A developer-facing visualization of the live z-machine object tree (and/or a world map) rendered with a modern lib, gated behind ?debug=1 where dev tooling belongs so it never touches the immersion-first player UI. Would need new wasm-bindgen exports for object-tree introspection (the removed debug_object_details was a starting point). Build against the current wasm/ crate + apps/web, not the old toolchain. Low priority. Related: [[h2g2-tqe]].

title: Write contribution guidelines (CONTRIBUTING.md)
description: Product objective. Provide clear contribution guidelines to facilitate high-quality community contributions. Cover dev setup (mise + just), test expectations (new features MUST include tests), style conventions (Google JS/TS), and the Adamsesque tone for user-facing copy.

title: Add MIDI background music and sound effects
description: Roadmap feature (from conductor product guide). Add MIDI audio support to deepen retro immersion. Should align with the retro terminal aesthetic and be unobtrusive/toggleable.

title: Add ASCII art integration for scenes and objects
description: Roadmap feature (from conductor product guide). Add varied-complexity ASCII art: minimalist symbolic icons for items, elaborate scene-setting headers for new locations, and animated elements for high-impact events. All assets must adhere to the terminal's phosphor-green/amber palette and mono-spaced constraints.
